library.description: Runtime-neutral supervision for execution units and coroutines.

blocks.text: Runtime-neutral supervision for execution units. The root entry owns unit budgets, attempts, active-unit lifecycle, bounded teardown, restart policy, health checks, capability admission, and observation. The `./coroutine` entry adds cooperative tasks; other unit profiles use the same root contracts.

Create a budget with `createUnitBudget({ kind, maxUnits })`, then pass that budget, a matching profile, a launcher, a specification, and a `report` callback to `createSupervisor`. Call `start()` and use the unit only when its result is `ready`. Call `dispose()` when finished. The complete coroutine example is in USEGUIDE.md.

The launcher must fulfill `handle.exited` only after its unit has stopped and its own resources are closed. `exited` never rejects. The profile validates specifications, declares required capabilities, terminates idempotently, and classifies fulfilled exit statuses. `report` receives terminal, cleanup, late rejection, and degraded-capability diagnostics. A health check that rejects its own failure while responding to cancellation is still reported after monitor closure; the exact cancellation reason need not be reported again. `inspect()` and `subscribe()` expose state without creating a unit.

Budgets return `{ kind: 'granted', lease }` or `{ kind: 'rejected', reason }`. Release each granted lease once; `release()` is idempotent. Closing a budget rejects pending and future admissions while existing leases remain held until their units actually exit. Nested budgets share the unit kind and release parent before child.

The default startup timeout is 10 seconds. A startup timeout follows the same restart/terminal policy as other startup failures and publishes a stable readiness result; acquireUnit failures are LAUNCH_FAILED with the original cause, even before a lease exists. Stop uses 5 seconds each for drain, graceful exit, and force reap. Restart defaults to `on-failure`, with 250 ms initial delay, factor 2, 30 seconds maximum delay, five restarts in 60 seconds. The default terminal policy stays terminal until explicit restart; a configured cooldown schedules one unref'd retry. Health checks default to a 5 second interval, 2 second check timeout, and three consecutive failures. Budget defaults are queue overflow, 30 second queue timeout, and eight grants per second. Supply a scheduler for deterministic timing.

The core depends only on `@migaia/lifecycle` and `@migaia/utils`. A profile may use `hooks.acquireUnit` for a preacquired unit, `hooks.afterLaunch` to own attachments, `hooks.onReady` to own monitors or fail the unit, and `hooks.inspectUnit` for a read-only snapshot. Attachments registered in `unit.scope` release after `exited`; monitors registered in `unit.monitors` release before termination. Unit-specific entry points belong beside, never inside, the root implementation.

Supervisor-created failures carry `source: '@migaia/supervision'` and one semantic `SupervisionErrorCode`; wrapped original failures remain on `cause`, and cleanup failures remain reachable through `errors`. Passive observer and late-check failures sent to `report` retain their original objects. States and budget outcomes are values, not thrown codes.

The `./process` entry adds a shell-free specification, capability checks, usage monitoring, bounded output tails, durable orphan records and recovery, a parent-loss guard, and an optional bounded prewarm pool. It defines a launcher port and does not start an operating-system process itself. See USEGUIDE.md for the process contract, defaults and cleanup.

The `./threads` entry supervises a launcher-owned thread with the same core budget, restart, health, replacement, and bounded release policy. The launcher declares `heap-limit` and `exit-observation` as `enforced` or `unsupported`; a launcher without enforced exit observation requires a health check. A thread is not a fault-isolation or CPU-limit boundary. Choose the process profile when either guarantee is required. See USEGUIDE.md for the thread launcher contract and example.
`health.intervalMs` must be finite and greater than zero, so recurring health checks cannot run at a zero interval.
`startupTimeoutMs` may be zero for an immediate one-shot startup deadline.
`restart` selects a supported mode and bounded exponential backoff; unknown modes fail option admission.
`terminalPolicy` selects stay or cooldown; unknown modes fail option admission.
`isolation` accepts required or best-effort; unknown modes fail option admission.
`stop` defines drain, exit and reap phases. Their one-shot budgets may be zero for an immediate deadline.

An unknown replacement strategy throws coded `INVALID_OPTION` before enqueuing or retiring the serving unit. The prewarm pool snapshots its injected scheduler through the same lifecycle admission as the supervisor.

`expose(port)` may be called once. A second call throws a coded `TypeError` inside the task. If the task ends before exposure, `exposed` remains pending, so the readiness hook waits until the startup deadline. The task's own signal aborts on stop, replacement, and dispose. Async generators also receive one `return()` request. `exited` always fulfills with `{ outcome: 'fulfilled' }` or `{ outcome: 'rejected', error }`. For a custom AsyncIterable, a rejected return request is reported immediately, but exited remains pending until the outstanding next finishes. Its lease is retained until that actual exit.

Cooperative termination depends on the task settling. A task that ignores cancellation can outlive the 5 second reap deadline. The supervisor reports `REAP_TIMEOUT`, records `abandoned`, and retains its budget lease until the task actually exits. It cannot preempt a synchronous loop or isolate a crash from the event loop. The `fault-isolation` capability is therefore `unsupported`; requests for it are rejected under the default `isolation: 'required'` policy.

`replace({ strategy: 'start-then-switch' })` needs a budget with room for two concurrent units. The old port stays usable until the candidate is ready and the `switched` event fires; then the old task receives cancellation. `replace({ spec })` validates the new specification before touching the active unit. The default strategy stops the old unit before launching the new one.

Use `heartbeat: { timeoutMs, intervalMs?, failureThreshold? }` when the task calls `heartbeat()` or yields from an async generator. A missed heartbeat becomes `UNHEALTHY` with `HEARTBEAT_MISSED` on its cause chain. `heartbeat` and the generic `health` option are mutually exclusive.

sections.heading: Advanced usage: a supervised process profile

blocks.text: `@migaia/supervision/process` is a platform-neutral contract. Supply an adapter whose `launch(spec, context)` starts without a shell, transfers only the named `env.inherit` keys plus `env.set`, drains every `drain` stream from startup through `context.output`, and fulfills `handle.exited` only after the unit and adapter-owned resources have closed. The adapter must generate a fingerprint that changes across pid reuse, terminate the declared process tree idempotently, and report capability strengths honestly. The profile itself never calls a platform spawn API.

The default isolation is `required`; a missing `termination` or `fault-isolation` guarantee rejects construction with `CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED`. A caller may explicitly select `best-effort` and inspect `degraded`, but this does not improve the adapter's actual guarantees. A monitored memory or CPU limit requires `sampleUsage`; sampling defaults to 1 second. Three consecutive sampleUsage rejections mark the unit unhealthy; a successful sample exceeding a monitored limit terminates it immediately. The supervisor and prewarm pool both require a finite positive usage.intervalMs and a positive safe-integer failureThreshold. Each output tail keeps the latest 65,536 bytes per stream. The parent-loss guard defaults to a 5 second shutdown grace period; prewarm idle units default to 60 seconds.

Bootstrap bytes travel only as a stdin prefix or dedicated fd. Never put them in arguments, environment, errors, snapshots or logs. The adapter must declare `bootstrap-stdin` or `bootstrap-fd` as `unsupported` when it cannot prove that carrier safe. Electron `utilityProcess` currently has neither approved bootstrap carrier. Windows tree termination may be declared `enforced` only after an adapter has proved creation inside a Job Object, or suspended creation followed by assignment and resume, including failure cleanup. The profile's in-memory tests do not establish those platform guarantees.

For durable recovery, inject a registry and call `reclaimOrphanProcesses` before creating a supervisor or pool. Recovery terminates only a record whose fingerprint still matches; reused pids are removed without termination. Each failed record stays available for another attempt. An optional prewarm pool uses the same budget, launcher and specification objects as its supervisor. It starts idle units but the supervisor still performs readiness after taking one. `restart()` and `replace()` bypass stale idle units. When pool and supervisor use the same id, registry port and namespace, adoption reuses the exact warm durable record and its actual-exit cleanup. Distinct owners register their own records. Output sink exceptions during buffered replay or live forwarding are reported without stopping delivery. A registry list failure is collected and reported as ORPHAN_RECLAIM_FAILED with detail.step set to list; no record is touched.

`@migaia/supervision/threads` owns a runtime-neutral thread contract. Supply a launcher whose `launch(spec, context)` creates a thread and returns an idempotently terminable handle. Its `exited` promise must fulfill only after thread code stops executing, and must never reject. An error event that leaves a Web-style thread running requires the adapter to terminate it and fulfill `exited` with `{ code: null, error }`. A termination request or a runtime close marker alone is not evidence of actual exit. If `context.signal` is already aborted, the launcher must reject without creating a thread.

The launcher must declare `termination: 'enforced' | 'monitored' | 'unsupported'` and `fault-isolation: 'unsupported'` truthfully. Required isolation accepts enforced or monitored termination, and rejects unsupported termination; a monitored declaration does not promise native enforcement. It also declares `heap-limit: 'enforced' | 'unsupported'`, and `exit-observation: 'enforced' | 'unsupported'` truthfully. `heapBytes` is accepted only when `heap-limit` is enforced; `callWallTimeMs` is passed unchanged to the launcher for its caller-facing operations. A launcher without enforced exit observation requires a `health` check so a silent exit or stalled thread can be stopped. The supervisor performs no heap sampling and has no separate graceful thread phase: it drains the optional `beforeTerminate` hook, requests `terminate()` once, then waits up to the core reap deadline for actual exit. An unconfirmed exit keeps its budget lease occupied.

Use `@migaia/supervision/process` when you need crash isolation, a CPU limit, durable orphan recovery, or output draining. Thread code shares the host process and cannot provide those guarantees. Platform adapters and their runtime-specific proof belong to their owning module; this profile does not assert that Bun, Deno, browser, or Electron thread termination has been verified by its in-memory tests.
`health.intervalMs` must be finite and greater than zero, so recurring health checks cannot run at a zero interval.
`startupTimeoutMs` may be zero for an immediate one-shot startup deadline.
`restart` selects a supported mode and bounded exponential backoff; unknown modes fail option admission.
`terminalPolicy` selects stay or cooldown; unknown modes fail option admission.
`isolation` accepts required or best-effort; unknown modes fail option admission.
`stop` defines drain, exit and reap phases. Their one-shot budgets may be zero for an immediate deadline.

An unknown replacement strategy throws coded `INVALID_OPTION` before enqueuing or retiring the serving unit. The prewarm pool snapshots its injected scheduler through the same lifecycle admission as the supervisor.

symbols.purpose: Creates a shared runtime-neutral capacity and launch-rate budget. Pair with createSupervisor or profile constructors; retain leases until actual unit exit.
symbols.core:
An `IUnitBudget`; invalid numeric limits or parent-kind mismatch throw coded `INVALID_OPTION` before admission starts.
kind: Choose which kind of work this budget counts: processes, threads or coroutines, where a coroutine is a task running within the current runtime. Set kind when creating the budget so unrelated resource types do not share capacity. If parent is supplied, its kind must match; a mismatch makes construction throw TypeError.
maxUnits: Finite nonnegative integer local concurrency cap; zero admits no unit.
overflow: Explicit reject refuses full capacity immediately; queue waits in FIFO order.
Omitted: queues in the current implementation; set reject explicitly for immediate refusal.
queueTimeoutMs: Finite positive scheduler deadline for a queued acquisition; expiry is a queue-timeout result.
`30000` milliseconds for each acquisition.
launchRate: Sliding grant rate independent of concurrent capacity; false disables rate limiting.
`{ max: 8, windowMs: 1000 }` grants eight leases per second.
Disable launch-rate limiting while retaining concurrency limits.
launchRate.max: Positive integer maximum successful grants in one sliding launch-rate window.
launchRate.windowMs: Finite positive scheduler length of the sliding grant-rate window.
parent: Optional matching-kind budget obtained from another createUnitBudget call; the lease composes both slots.
Absent: only local admission is applied.
scheduler: Monotonic clock and timers supplied by the application; see `IScheduler` in `@migaia/utils/scheduler`.
`systemScheduler`; uses the host timers.

symbols.core:
state: Current lifecycle state read synchronously without launching or checking the unit.
generation: Attempt generation used to correlate commands and events; it does not count successful restarts.
start: Starts or joins readiness; construction creates no native unit. Startup timeout follows the configured failure policy, while acquireUnit rejection becomes LAUNCH_FAILED with cause even before a lease exists.
An `IReadyOutcome`; disposal rejects with `SCOPE_CLOSED` or `SCOPE_TERMINAL`.
whenReady: Observes stable readiness without starting a new command; cancellation rejects with the caller signal reason.
whenReady.signal: Optional application cancellation signal; abort affects this wait only.

stop: Drains and retires current work; concurrent calls share the pending stop Promise, and the supervisor can later start again.
stop.options: Optional `ISupervisorStopOptions` from the caller; graceMs overrides application drain only.
Resolves after bounded teardown; abandoned actual work retains its lease.
kill: Upgrades the existing teardown to force immediately; joining callers keep the original pending stop Promise.
Resolves after the same bounded stop sequence.
restart: Resets recent restart failures, retires the active unit and launches a fresh attempt.
Readiness outcome for the fresh attempt; disposal rejects with a scope error.
replace: Replaces an active unit with the same or a new spec; invalid strategy throws `INVALID_OPTION` before changing the serving unit.
replace.options: Replacement options: default stop-then-start and current spec. Start-then-switch needs another slot; the serving unit remains owned by its active slot after startup attempt completion. Only candidate readiness and the switched event permit cancelling the old task.
`IReplaceOutcome` reports replacement, admission refusal, or failure without hiding the original error.
inspect: Reads diagnostics without sampling native resources or modifying lifecycle state.
An `ISupervisorSnapshot` of current state and contained failures.
subscribe: Registers a synchronous event observer; it receives `ISupervisorEvent` changes and observer throws are reported.
subscribe.listener: Application callback receives a discriminated event, returns void synchronously, and should not throw.
Idempotent removal function for this observer only.
dispose: Closes admission permanently and joins bounded retirement; repeated in-flight calls share one disposal Promise.
Resolves when disposal reaches its terminal state; future unit-producing commands reject.

symbols.purpose: Shared readiness, restart, drain and health policy used by every execution profile.
symbols.core:
id: Nonempty stable name chosen by the application for diagnostics and durable process ownership.
report: Application callback receiving each contained launch, health, cleanup or late error; returns void synchronously and must not throw. Late health-check failure remains reported after monitor closure; only the exact abort reason is suppressed, and passive failures retain the original object.
ready: Optional asynchronous handshake receiving the launched handle and attempt cancellation signal; resolve to admit readiness, reject or throw to fail startup.
Absent: launch completion is readiness.
startupTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative launch-plus-readiness deadline in scheduler milliseconds; zero expires immediately. Expiry retires the attempt and follows normal restart/terminal policy, publishing a stable outcome instead of leaving the supervisor starting.
`10000` milliseconds for each attempt.
restart: Automatic restart policy for classified exits; nested fields control mode, backoff and the failure window.
An empty policy uses the nested defaults below.
restart.mode: Chooses which actual exits schedule an automatic restart; manual restart remains available.
`on-failure`; normal completion stops.
restart.initialDelayMs: Finite nonnegative first restart delay in scheduler milliseconds.
`250` milliseconds before the first retry.
restart.factor: Finite multiplier of successive restart delays; must be at least one.
`2`; each failure doubles the delay until its cap.
restart.maxDelayMs: Finite nonnegative upper bound of exponential retry delay in milliseconds.
`30000` milliseconds caps backoff.
restart.maxRestarts: Nonnegative safe integer controlling failures admitted in one sliding restart window.
`5` failures before exhaustion.
restart.windowMs: Finite nonnegative scheduler window for counting recent failures.
`60000` milliseconds of failure history.
terminalPolicy: After exhaustion, keeps terminal admission closed or schedules an explicit cooldown.
Absent: remain terminal until explicit restart.
terminalPolicy.mode: Selects a terminal wait until explicit restart or a timed cooldown retry after exhaustion; only disposal permanently closes the supervisor.
terminalPolicy.afterMs: Finite nonnegative cooldown duration required only for the cooldown policy.
stop: Ordered application drain, graceful exit and forced reap phases for each retiring unit.
Absent: each phase uses its nested default.
stop.beforeTerminate: Asynchronous application drain receiving handle, native cancellation signal and remainingMs getter; resolve when drained. Failure is reported and termination proceeds.
Absent: skip application draining work.
stop.drainTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative maximum application drain time; a command graceMs overrides this phase only.
`5000` milliseconds for application drain.
stop.exitTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative wait for actual graceful exit before requesting force.
`5000` milliseconds before force.
stop.reapTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative recovery wait after force; a timed-out unit keeps its lease until actual exit.
`5000` milliseconds of forced recovery.
health: Serial periodic checks for ready handles; consecutive failures invalidate the generation.
Absent: no health monitor is installed.
health.check: Application asynchronous check receiving the current handle and cancellation signal; resolve if healthy, reject or throw to count failure.
health.intervalMs: Finite positive interval between serial checks, measured by the scheduler.
`5000` milliseconds between checks.
health.timeoutMs: Finite nonnegative deadline for one health check before recording failure.
`2000` milliseconds for one check.
health.failureThreshold: Nonnegative safe integer threshold of consecutive failed checks that invalidates readiness.
`3` consecutive failures invalidate the unit.
isolation: Required admission accepts enforced or monitored capabilities; best effort records weaker guarantees as degradation.
`required`; insufficient capabilities fail construction.
requires: Additional capability names chosen by the application, merged with profile requirements before admission.
An empty list adds no capability requirements.
scheduler: Monotonic clock and timers supplied by the application; see `IScheduler` in `@migaia/utils/scheduler`.
`systemScheduler`; uses the host timers.
parameters: This type declaration has no parameters.
symbols.returns: No explicit return annotation is declared for this type.

type: SupervisorEventType selecting the event-specific payload fields.
from: Previous lifecycle state for state events, or previous generation for switched events.
to: Next lifecycle state for state events, or newly active generation for switched events.
generation: Attempt generation used to correlate commands and events; it does not count successful restarts.
reason: Profile or command exit classification carried only by exit events.
error: Original contained failure carried by failed exit or terminal events.
status: Optional actual native IUnitExitStatus supplied by the profile.
observedAt: Scheduler observation timestamp, measured in monotonic milliseconds.
entry: Lifetime terminal-entry ordinal carried by a terminal event.
unit: Launcher-created newly active handle carried by a switched event.
count: Lifetime successful restart count carried by a restart event.
degraded: Admitted degraded capability names carried when their set changes.

id: Nonempty stable name chosen by the application for diagnostics and durable process ownership.
report: Application callback receiving each contained launch, health, cleanup or late error; returns void synchronously and must not throw. Late health-check failure remains reported after monitor closure; only the exact abort reason is suppressed, and passive failures retain the original object.
ready: Optional asynchronous handshake receiving the launched handle and attempt cancellation signal; resolve to admit readiness, reject or throw to fail startup.
Absent: launch completion is readiness.
startupTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative launch-plus-readiness deadline in scheduler milliseconds; zero expires immediately. Expiry retires the attempt and follows normal restart/terminal policy, publishing a stable outcome instead of leaving the supervisor starting.
`10000` milliseconds for each attempt.
restart: Automatic restart policy for classified exits; nested fields control mode, backoff and the failure window.
An empty policy uses the nested defaults below.
restart.mode: Chooses which actual exits schedule an automatic restart; manual restart remains available.
`on-failure`; normal completion stops.
restart.initialDelayMs: Finite nonnegative first restart delay in scheduler milliseconds.
`250` milliseconds before the first retry.
restart.factor: Finite multiplier of successive restart delays; must be at least one.

restart.maxDelayMs: Finite nonnegative upper bound of exponential retry delay in milliseconds.
`30000` milliseconds caps backoff.
restart.maxRestarts: Nonnegative safe integer controlling failures admitted in one sliding restart window.
`5` failures before exhaustion.
restart.windowMs: Finite nonnegative scheduler window for counting recent failures.
`60000` milliseconds of failure history.
terminalPolicy: After exhaustion, keeps terminal admission closed or schedules an explicit cooldown.

terminalPolicy.mode: Selects a terminal wait until explicit restart or a timed cooldown retry after exhaustion; only disposal permanently closes the supervisor.
terminalPolicy.afterMs: Finite nonnegative cooldown duration required only for the cooldown policy.
stop: Ordered application drain, graceful exit and forced reap phases for each retiring unit.
Absent: each phase uses its nested default.
stop.beforeTerminate: Asynchronous application drain receiving handle, native cancellation signal and remainingMs getter; resolve when drained. Failure is reported and termination proceeds.
Absent: skip application draining work.
stop.drainTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative maximum application drain time; a command graceMs overrides this phase only.

pending: Unresolved acquire calls including the active FIFO queue head.
closed: Whether admission has permanently closed; existing occupied leases remain valid.
close: Rejects waiting and future acquisitions; existing leases remain occupied until their owners release them.

startupTimeout: STARTUP_TIMEOUT: startup missed its deadline. Bounded retirement advances to the configured backoff, stopped or terminal policy without leaking a temporary terminal event or leaving starting stuck; readiness receives a stable failed result.
exitUnexpected: `EXIT_UNEXPECTED`: unexpected actual exit; inspect native status and original cause.
unhealthy: `UNHEALTHY`: health failures crossed the threshold; the generation is invalidated.
resourceLimitExceeded: `RESOURCE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`: resource monitoring observed a limit breach; inspect the limit detail.
reapTimeout: `REAP_TIMEOUT`: recovery deadline ended before actual exit; the lease remains occupied.

scopeTerminal: `SCOPE_TERMINAL`: a unit-producing command ran after disposal; create a new supervisor.
heartbeatMissed: `HEARTBEAT_MISSED`: a coroutine heartbeat became stale; inspect cooperative task progress.

sections.title: 核心用法
sections.content:
invalidOption: `INVALID_OPTION`: invalid constructor, specification or command option; correct the named field before retrying.
capabilityUnsupported: `CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED`: required capability lacks a sufficient guarantee; change launcher or isolation policy.
launchFailed: LAUNCH_FAILED: preacquisition, launch, attachment or readiness failed. An acquireUnit failure before lease acquisition still returns a controlled failed readiness outcome and follows the configured failure policy; inspect phase and preserved cause.
startupTimeout: STARTUP_TIMEOUT: startup missed its deadline. Bounded retirement advances to the configured backoff, stopped or terminal policy without leaking a temporary terminal event or leaving starting stuck; readiness receives a stable failed result.
exitUnexpected: `EXIT_UNEXPECTED`: unexpected actual exit; inspect native status and original cause.
unhealthy: `UNHEALTHY`: health failures crossed the threshold; the generation is invalidated.
resourceLimitExceeded: `RESOURCE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`: resource monitoring observed a limit breach; inspect the limit detail.
reapTimeout: `REAP_TIMEOUT`: recovery deadline ended before actual exit; the lease remains occupied.
supervisionExhausted: `SUPERVISION_EXHAUSTED`: restart window exhausted; inspect terminal error before explicit restart.
scopeClosed: `SCOPE_CLOSED`: a unit-producing command ran during disposal; wait for completion.
scopeTerminal: `SCOPE_TERMINAL`: a unit-producing command ran after disposal; create a new supervisor.
heartbeatMissed: `HEARTBEAT_MISSED`: a coroutine heartbeat became stale; inspect cooperative task progress.
orphanReclaimFailed: ORPHAN_RECLAIM_FAILED: registry listing or a per-record probe/termination/removal failed. Listing failure is collected and reported with detail.step=list and original cause; no record is touched. Failed records remain available for retry.

symbols.name: createCoroutineSupervisor
symbols.signature: export declare function createCoroutineSupervisor<TPort = undefined>(options: ICoroutineSupervisorOptions<TPort>): ICoroutineSupervisor<TPort>;
symbols.purpose: Supervises a cooperative task or async iterator without native process isolation. Task cancellation is cooperative; an unending task keeps its budget lease after bounded recovery.
symbols.core:
An `ICoroutineSupervisor`; invalid task or simultaneous heartbeat and health policies throw `INVALID_OPTION`.
id: Nonempty stable name chosen by the application for diagnostics and durable process ownership.
report: Application callback receiving each contained launch, health, cleanup or late error; returns void synchronously and must not throw. Late health-check failure remains reported after monitor closure; only the exact abort reason is suppressed, and passive failures retain the original object.
ready: Optional asynchronous handshake receiving the launched handle and attempt cancellation signal; resolve to admit readiness, reject or throw to fail startup.
Absent: launch completion is readiness.
startupTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative launch-plus-readiness deadline in scheduler milliseconds; zero expires immediately. Expiry retires the attempt and follows normal restart/terminal policy, publishing a stable outcome instead of leaving the supervisor starting.
`10000` milliseconds for each attempt.
restart: Automatic restart policy for classified exits; nested fields control mode, backoff and the failure window.

isolation: Required admission accepts enforced or monitored capabilities; best effort records weaker guarantees as degradation.
`required`; insufficient capabilities fail construction.
requires: Additional capability names chosen by the application, merged with profile requirements before admission.
An empty list adds no capability requirements.
startupTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative launch-plus-readiness deadline in scheduler milliseconds; zero expires immediately. Expiry retires the attempt and follows normal restart/terminal policy, publishing a stable outcome instead of leaving the supervisor starting.

scheduler: Monotonic clock and timers supplied by the application; see `IScheduler` in `@migaia/utils/scheduler`.

launcher: Runtime adapter supplied by the application; its launch result must settle exited only after execution and resources stop.
spec: Initial application specification validated by the selected unit profile before admission.
budget: Shared matching-kind budget returned by `createUnitBudget`; actual exit releases its occupied lease.
registry: Application durable record port and namespace for recovering prior-run process identities.

symbols.name: createProcessSupervisor
symbols.signature: export declare function createProcessSupervisor<THandle extends IProcessHandle>(options: IProcessSupervisorOptions<THandle>): IProcessSupervisor<THandle>;
symbols.purpose: Supervises shell-free native processes through an injected launcher, with optional resource monitoring, bounded output tails and durable ownership records.
symbols.core:
An `IProcessSupervisor`; invalid closed specification throws `INVALID_OPTION`, unsupported capabilities fail before launch.
id: Nonempty stable name chosen by the application for diagnostics and durable process ownership.
report: Application callback receiving each contained launch, health, cleanup or late error; returns void synchronously and must not throw. Late health-check failure remains reported after monitor closure; only the exact abort reason is suppressed, and passive failures retain the original object.
ready: Optional asynchronous handshake receiving the launched handle and attempt cancellation signal; resolve to admit readiness, reject or throw to fail startup.
Absent: launch completion is readiness.
startupTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative launch-plus-readiness deadline in scheduler milliseconds; zero expires immediately. Expiry retires the attempt and follows normal restart/terminal policy, publishing a stable outcome instead of leaving the supervisor starting.
`10000` milliseconds for each attempt.
restart: Automatic restart policy for classified exits; nested fields control mode, backoff and the failure window.
An empty policy uses the nested defaults below.
restart.mode: Chooses which actual exits schedule an automatic restart; manual restart remains available.
`on-failure`; normal completion stops.
restart.initialDelayMs: Finite nonnegative first restart delay in scheduler milliseconds.
`250` milliseconds before the first retry.
restart.factor: Finite multiplier of successive restart delays; must be at least one.
`2`; each failure doubles the delay until its cap.
restart.maxDelayMs: Finite nonnegative upper bound of exponential retry delay in milliseconds.
`30000` milliseconds caps backoff.
restart.maxRestarts: Nonnegative safe integer controlling failures admitted in one sliding restart window.
`5` failures before exhaustion.
restart.windowMs: Finite nonnegative scheduler window for counting recent failures.
`60000` milliseconds of failure history.
terminalPolicy: After exhaustion, keeps terminal admission closed or schedules an explicit cooldown.
Absent: remain terminal until explicit restart.
terminalPolicy.mode: Selects a terminal wait until explicit restart or a timed cooldown retry after exhaustion; only disposal permanently closes the supervisor.
terminalPolicy.afterMs: Finite nonnegative cooldown duration required only for the cooldown policy.
stop: Ordered application drain, graceful exit and forced reap phases for each retiring unit.
Absent: each phase uses its nested default.
stop.beforeTerminate: Asynchronous application drain receiving handle, native cancellation signal and remainingMs getter; resolve when drained. Failure is reported and termination proceeds.
Absent: skip application draining work.
stop.drainTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative maximum application drain time; a command graceMs overrides this phase only.
`5000` milliseconds for application drain.
stop.exitTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative wait for actual graceful exit before requesting force.
`5000` milliseconds before force.
stop.reapTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative recovery wait after force; a timed-out unit keeps its lease until actual exit.
`5000` milliseconds of forced recovery.
health: Serial periodic checks for ready handles; consecutive failures invalidate the generation.
Absent: no health monitor is installed.
health.check: Application asynchronous check receiving the current handle and cancellation signal; resolve if healthy, reject or throw to count failure.
health.intervalMs: Finite positive interval between serial checks, measured by the scheduler.
`5000` milliseconds between checks.
health.timeoutMs: Finite nonnegative deadline for one health check before recording failure.
`2000` milliseconds for one check.
health.failureThreshold: Nonnegative safe integer threshold of consecutive failed checks that invalidates readiness.
`3` consecutive failures invalidate the unit.
isolation: Required admission accepts enforced or monitored capabilities; best effort records weaker guarantees as degradation.
`required`; insufficient capabilities fail construction.
requires: Additional capability names chosen by the application, merged with profile requirements before admission.
An empty list adds no capability requirements.
scheduler: Monotonic clock and timers supplied by the application; see `IScheduler` in `@migaia/utils/scheduler`.
`systemScheduler`; uses the host timers.
launcher: Runtime adapter supplied by the application; its launch result must settle exited only after execution and resources stop.
spec: Initial application specification validated by the selected unit profile before admission.
budget: Shared matching-kind budget returned by `createUnitBudget`; actual exit releases its occupied lease.
usage: Native resource sampling policy used when process memory or CPU limits are monitored.
Absent: samples use interval and threshold defaults.
usage.intervalMs: Finite positive scheduler interval for native process resource samples. Both supervisor and prewarm pool reject zero/nonfinite intervals and nonpositive or unsafe failure thresholds as RangeError/INVALID_OPTION.
`1000` milliseconds between samples.
usage.failureThreshold: Positive safe-integer count of consecutive sampleUsage rejections before the process is unhealthy. A successful sample resets this count; a successful sample exceeding a monitored limit terminates immediately.
`3` consecutive sampleUsage rejections, not three successful over-limit samples.
output: Bounds diagnostic stdout and stderr tails while launchers continue draining regardless of observers.
Absent: retain bounded tails without a chunk observer.
output.tailBytes: Positive safe-integer maximum bytes retained separately per output stream; zero is invalid and does not disable tail capture.
`65536` bytes for each stream.
output.onChunk: Synchronous observer receives stream label and drained bytes; returns void and does not own draining. Throws are reported.
Absent: only bounded diagnostic tails are retained.
registry: Application durable record port and namespace for recovering prior-run process identities.
Absent: no durable records or orphan recovery.
registry.port: Application storage implementing `IProcessRegistry`; add and removal follow actual process ownership.
registry.namespace: Application chosen isolation name; recovery lists only records in this namespace.
prewarm: Pool from createPrewarmPool with matching budget, launcher and spec; transfers the idle handle and lease. Matching id, registry port and namespace reuse the exact warm durable record and its actual-exit cleanup; different owners create their own records.
Absent: launch every admitted process cold.
wallClock: Epoch clock supplied by the application for durable launch timestamps; not used for deadlines.

sections.title: 介绍
sections.content: Supervises shell-free native processes through an injected launcher, with optional resource monitoring, bounded output tails and durable ownership records.

sections.title: 上手
sections.content: Import createProcessSupervisor from @migaia/supervision/process, then follow a maintained task example for your use case.

sections.title: 适用场景
sections.content: Use createProcessSupervisor when its function contract and declared inputs match the result you need. Choose a different public symbol when createProcessSupervisor does not match the required inputs or return contract.

sections.title: 快速实现
sections.content: Use a maintained function example that demonstrates real inputs and observable behavior.

sections.title: 核心用法
sections.content:
An `IProcessSupervisor`; invalid closed specification throws `INVALID_OPTION`, unsupported capabilities fail before launch.
id: Nonempty stable name chosen by the application for diagnostics and durable process ownership.
report: Application callback receiving each contained launch, health, cleanup or late error; returns void synchronously and must not throw. Late health-check failure remains reported after monitor closure; only the exact abort reason is suppressed, and passive failures retain the original object.
ready: Optional asynchronous handshake receiving the launched handle and attempt cancellation signal; resolve to admit readiness, reject or throw to fail startup.
Absent: launch completion is readiness.
startupTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative launch-plus-readiness deadline in scheduler milliseconds; zero expires immediately. Expiry retires the attempt and follows normal restart/terminal policy, publishing a stable outcome instead of leaving the supervisor starting.
`10000` milliseconds for each attempt.
restart: Automatic restart policy for classified exits; nested fields control mode, backoff and the failure window.
An empty policy uses the nested defaults below.
restart.mode: Chooses which actual exits schedule an automatic restart; manual restart remains available.
`on-failure`; normal completion stops.
restart.initialDelayMs: Finite nonnegative first restart delay in scheduler milliseconds.
`250` milliseconds before the first retry.
restart.factor: Finite multiplier of successive restart delays; must be at least one.
`2`; each failure doubles the delay until its cap.
restart.maxDelayMs: Finite nonnegative upper bound of exponential retry delay in milliseconds.
`30000` milliseconds caps backoff.
restart.maxRestarts: Nonnegative safe integer controlling failures admitted in one sliding restart window.
`5` failures before exhaustion.
restart.windowMs: Finite nonnegative scheduler window for counting recent failures.
`60000` milliseconds of failure history.
terminalPolicy: After exhaustion, keeps terminal admission closed or schedules an explicit cooldown.
Absent: remain terminal until explicit restart.
terminalPolicy.mode: Selects a terminal wait until explicit restart or a timed cooldown retry after exhaustion; only disposal permanently closes the supervisor.
terminalPolicy.afterMs: Finite nonnegative cooldown duration required only for the cooldown policy.
stop: Ordered application drain, graceful exit and forced reap phases for each retiring unit.
Absent: each phase uses its nested default.
stop.beforeTerminate: Asynchronous application drain receiving handle, native cancellation signal and remainingMs getter; resolve when drained. Failure is reported and termination proceeds.
Absent: skip application draining work.
stop.drainTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative maximum application drain time; a command graceMs overrides this phase only.
`5000` milliseconds for application drain.
stop.exitTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative wait for actual graceful exit before requesting force.
`5000` milliseconds before force.
stop.reapTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative recovery wait after force; a timed-out unit keeps its lease until actual exit.
`5000` milliseconds of forced recovery.
health: Serial periodic checks for ready handles; consecutive failures invalidate the generation.
Absent: no health monitor is installed.
health.check: Application asynchronous check receiving the current handle and cancellation signal; resolve if healthy, reject or throw to count failure.
health.intervalMs: Finite positive interval between serial checks, measured by the scheduler.
`5000` milliseconds between checks.
health.timeoutMs: Finite nonnegative deadline for one health check before recording failure.
`2000` milliseconds for one check.
health.failureThreshold: Nonnegative safe integer threshold of consecutive failed checks that invalidates readiness.
`3` consecutive failures invalidate the unit.
isolation: Required admission accepts enforced or monitored capabilities; best effort records weaker guarantees as degradation.
`required`; insufficient capabilities fail construction.
requires: Additional capability names chosen by the application, merged with profile requirements before admission.
An empty list adds no capability requirements.
scheduler: Monotonic clock and timers supplied by the application; see `IScheduler` in `@migaia/utils/scheduler`.
`systemScheduler`; uses the host timers.
launcher: Runtime adapter supplied by the application; its launch result must settle exited only after execution and resources stop.
spec: Initial application specification validated by the selected unit profile before admission.
budget: Shared matching-kind budget returned by `createUnitBudget`; actual exit releases its occupied lease.
usage: Native resource sampling policy used when process memory or CPU limits are monitored.
Absent: samples use interval and threshold defaults.
usage.intervalMs: Finite positive scheduler interval for native process resource samples. Both supervisor and prewarm pool reject zero/nonfinite intervals and nonpositive or unsafe failure thresholds as RangeError/INVALID_OPTION.
`1000` milliseconds between samples.
usage.failureThreshold: Positive safe-integer count of consecutive sampleUsage rejections before the process is unhealthy. A successful sample resets this count; a successful sample exceeding a monitored limit terminates immediately.
`3` consecutive sampleUsage rejections, not three successful over-limit samples.
output: Bounds diagnostic stdout and stderr tails while launchers continue draining regardless of observers.
Absent: retain bounded tails without a chunk observer.
output.tailBytes: Positive safe-integer maximum bytes retained separately per output stream; zero is invalid and does not disable tail capture.
`65536` bytes for each stream.
output.onChunk: Synchronous observer receives stream label and drained bytes; returns void and does not own draining. Throws are reported.
Absent: only bounded diagnostic tails are retained.
registry: Application durable record port and namespace for recovering prior-run process identities.
Absent: no durable records or orphan recovery.
registry.port: Application storage implementing `IProcessRegistry`; add and removal follow actual process ownership.
registry.namespace: Application chosen isolation name; recovery lists only records in this namespace.
prewarm: Pool from createPrewarmPool with matching budget, launcher and spec; transfers the idle handle and lease. Matching id, registry port and namespace reuse the exact warm durable record and its actual-exit cleanup; different owners create their own records.
Absent: launch every admitted process cold.
wallClock: Epoch clock supplied by the application for durable launch timestamps; not used for deadlines.
`systemWallClock`; uses host epoch time.

configuration.name: launcher
configuration.description: For durable recovery, inject a registry and call `reclaimOrphanProcesses` before creating a supervisor or pool. Recovery terminates only a record whose fingerprint still matches; reused pids are removed without termination. Each failed record stays available for another attempt. An optional prewarm pool uses the same budget, launcher and specification objects as its supervisor. It starts idle units but the supervisor still performs readiness after taking one. `restart()` and `replace()` bypass stale idle units. When pool and supervisor use the same id, registry port and namespace, adoption reuses the exact warm durable record and its actual-exit cleanup. Distinct owners register their own records. Output sink exceptions during buffered replay or live forwarding are reported without stopping delivery. A registry list failure is collected and reported as ORPHAN_RECLAIM_FAILED with detail.step set to list; no record is touched.

symbols.name: IPrewarmPool
symbols.signature: export type IPrewarmPool<THandle extends IProcessHandle> = { readonly id: string; readonly spec: IProcessSpec; readonly budget: IProcessBudget; readonly launcher: IProcessLauncher<THandle>; readonly idle: number; take(): IPrewarmEntry<THandle> | undefined; invalidate(): void; dispose(): Promise<void>; };
symbols.purpose: Application-owned pool whose take transfers handle and lease ownership to its consumer.
symbols.core:
id: Application identifier supplied at pool construction.
spec: The process launch settings supplied when the pool was created, such as the command and its arguments. The pool passes them to its launcher to start idle processes ahead of a request, so a later caller can take an already-started process.
budget: The process-capacity budget supplied to the pool. Each idle process occupies one slot, represented by a lease: an object that records and later releases that capacity. Taking a process transfers its lease to the caller instead of freeing the slot. When the pool closes an idle process, the slot stays occupied until that process actually exits.
launcher: The runtime adapter that actually starts the pool processes. Its launch() result supplies an exited Promise, which must complete only after execution and associated resources have stopped. The pool uses that completion when deciding that a closed process no longer occupies capacity; merely requesting termination is not enough.
idle: Current number of ready idle entries still owned by the pool.
take: Synchronously transfers one ready idle entry and its occupied lease to the caller.
An `IPrewarmEntry`, or undefined when no eligible entry exists.
invalidate: Retires owned idle entries; already transferred entries remain owned by their consumers.
Idle entries begin retirement without synchronously awaiting actual exit.
dispose: Permanently closes the pool and awaits bounded teardown of every remaining owned entry.
Resolves after owned idle entries finish bounded retirement.

state: Current lifecycle state read synchronously without launching or checking the unit.
generation: Attempt generation used to correlate commands and events; it does not count successful restarts.
start: Starts or joins readiness; construction creates no native unit. Startup timeout follows the configured failure policy, while acquireUnit rejection becomes LAUNCH_FAILED with cause even before a lease exists.

whenReady: Observes stable readiness without starting a new command; cancellation rejects with the caller signal reason.

symbols.purpose: Process profile construction with optional usage monitoring, output tails, registry and prewarm adoption.
symbols.core:
id: Nonempty stable name chosen by the application for diagnostics and durable process ownership.
report: Application callback receiving each contained launch, health, cleanup or late error; returns void synchronously and must not throw. Late health-check failure remains reported after monitor closure; only the exact abort reason is suppressed, and passive failures retain the original object.
ready: Optional asynchronous handshake receiving the launched handle and attempt cancellation signal; resolve to admit readiness, reject or throw to fail startup.
Absent: launch completion is readiness.
startupTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative launch-plus-readiness deadline in scheduler milliseconds; zero expires immediately. Expiry retires the attempt and follows normal restart/terminal policy, publishing a stable outcome instead of leaving the supervisor starting.
`10000` milliseconds for each attempt.
restart: Automatic restart policy for classified exits; nested fields control mode, backoff and the failure window.
An empty policy uses the nested defaults below.
restart.mode: Chooses which actual exits schedule an automatic restart; manual restart remains available.
`on-failure`; normal completion stops.
restart.initialDelayMs: Finite nonnegative first restart delay in scheduler milliseconds.
`250` milliseconds before the first retry.
restart.factor: Finite multiplier of successive restart delays; must be at least one.
`2`; each failure doubles the delay until its cap.
restart.maxDelayMs: Finite nonnegative upper bound of exponential retry delay in milliseconds.
`30000` milliseconds caps backoff.
restart.maxRestarts: Nonnegative safe integer controlling failures admitted in one sliding restart window.
`5` failures before exhaustion.
restart.windowMs: Finite nonnegative scheduler window for counting recent failures.
`60000` milliseconds of failure history.
terminalPolicy: After exhaustion, keeps terminal admission closed or schedules an explicit cooldown.
Absent: remain terminal until explicit restart.
terminalPolicy.mode: Selects a terminal wait until explicit restart or a timed cooldown retry after exhaustion; only disposal permanently closes the supervisor.
terminalPolicy.afterMs: Finite nonnegative cooldown duration required only for the cooldown policy.
stop: Ordered application drain, graceful exit and forced reap phases for each retiring unit.
Absent: each phase uses its nested default.
stop.beforeTerminate: Asynchronous application drain receiving handle, native cancellation signal and remainingMs getter; resolve when drained. Failure is reported and termination proceeds.
Absent: skip application draining work.
stop.drainTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative maximum application drain time; a command graceMs overrides this phase only.
`5000` milliseconds for application drain.
stop.exitTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative wait for actual graceful exit before requesting force.
`5000` milliseconds before force.
stop.reapTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative recovery wait after force; a timed-out unit keeps its lease until actual exit.
`5000` milliseconds of forced recovery.
health: Serial periodic checks for ready handles; consecutive failures invalidate the generation.
Absent: no health monitor is installed.
health.check: Application asynchronous check receiving the current handle and cancellation signal; resolve if healthy, reject or throw to count failure.
health.intervalMs: Finite positive interval between serial checks, measured by the scheduler.
`5000` milliseconds between checks.
health.timeoutMs: Finite nonnegative deadline for one health check before recording failure.
`2000` milliseconds for one check.
health.failureThreshold: Nonnegative safe integer threshold of consecutive failed checks that invalidates readiness.
`3` consecutive failures invalidate the unit.
isolation: Required admission accepts enforced or monitored capabilities; best effort records weaker guarantees as degradation.
`required`; insufficient capabilities fail construction.
requires: Additional capability names chosen by the application, merged with profile requirements before admission.
An empty list adds no capability requirements.
scheduler: Monotonic clock and timers supplied by the application; see `IScheduler` in `@migaia/utils/scheduler`.
`systemScheduler`; uses the host timers.
launcher: Runtime adapter supplied by the application; its launch result must settle exited only after execution and resources stop.
spec: Initial application specification validated by the selected unit profile before admission.
budget: Shared matching-kind budget returned by `createUnitBudget`; actual exit releases its occupied lease.
usage: Native resource sampling policy used when process memory or CPU limits are monitored.
Absent: samples use interval and threshold defaults.
usage.intervalMs: Finite positive scheduler interval for native process resource samples. Both supervisor and prewarm pool reject zero/nonfinite intervals and nonpositive or unsafe failure thresholds as RangeError/INVALID_OPTION.
`1000` milliseconds between samples.
usage.failureThreshold: Positive safe-integer count of consecutive sampleUsage rejections before the process is unhealthy. A successful sample resets this count; a successful sample exceeding a monitored limit terminates immediately.
`3` consecutive sampleUsage rejections, not three successful over-limit samples.
output: Bounds diagnostic stdout and stderr tails while launchers continue draining regardless of observers.
Absent: retain bounded tails without a chunk observer.
output.tailBytes: Positive safe-integer maximum bytes retained separately per output stream; zero is invalid and does not disable tail capture.
`65536` bytes for each stream.
output.onChunk: Synchronous observer receives stream label and drained bytes; returns void and does not own draining. Throws are reported.
Absent: only bounded diagnostic tails are retained.
registry: Application durable record port and namespace for recovering prior-run process identities.
Absent: no durable records or orphan recovery.
registry.port: Application storage implementing `IProcessRegistry`; add and removal follow actual process ownership.
registry.namespace: Application chosen isolation name; recovery lists only records in this namespace.
prewarm: Pool from createPrewarmPool with matching budget, launcher and spec; transfers the idle handle and lease. Matching id, registry port and namespace reuse the exact warm durable record and its actual-exit cleanup; different owners create their own records.
Absent: launch every admitted process cold.
wallClock: Epoch clock supplied by the application for durable launch timestamps; not used for deadlines.
`systemWallClock`; uses host epoch time.

sections.content:
An `IThreadSupervisor`; invalid specification or unsupported isolation fails before native launch.
id: Nonempty stable name chosen by the application for diagnostics and durable process ownership.
report: Application callback receiving each contained launch, health, cleanup or late error; returns void synchronously and must not throw. Late health-check failure remains reported after monitor closure; only the exact abort reason is suppressed, and passive failures retain the original object.
ready: Optional asynchronous handshake receiving the launched handle and attempt cancellation signal; resolve to admit readiness, reject or throw to fail startup.
Absent: launch completion is readiness.
startupTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative launch-plus-readiness deadline in scheduler milliseconds; zero expires immediately. Expiry retires the attempt and follows normal restart/terminal policy, publishing a stable outcome instead of leaving the supervisor starting.
`10000` milliseconds for each attempt.
restart: Automatic restart policy for classified exits; nested fields control mode, backoff and the failure window.
An empty policy uses the nested defaults below.
restart.mode: Chooses which actual exits schedule an automatic restart; manual restart remains available.
`on-failure`; normal completion stops.
restart.initialDelayMs: Finite nonnegative first restart delay in scheduler milliseconds.
`250` milliseconds before the first retry.
restart.factor: Finite multiplier of successive restart delays; must be at least one.
`2`; each failure doubles the delay until its cap.
restart.maxDelayMs: Finite nonnegative upper bound of exponential retry delay in milliseconds.
`30000` milliseconds caps backoff.
restart.maxRestarts: Nonnegative safe integer controlling failures admitted in one sliding restart window.
`5` failures before exhaustion.
restart.windowMs: Finite nonnegative scheduler window for counting recent failures.
`60000` milliseconds of failure history.
terminalPolicy: After exhaustion, keeps terminal admission closed or schedules an explicit cooldown.
Absent: remain terminal until explicit restart.
terminalPolicy.mode: Selects a terminal wait until explicit restart or a timed cooldown retry after exhaustion; only disposal permanently closes the supervisor.
terminalPolicy.afterMs: Finite nonnegative cooldown duration required only for the cooldown policy.
stop: Ordered application drain, graceful exit and forced reap phases for each retiring unit.
Absent: each phase uses its nested default.
stop.beforeTerminate: Asynchronous application drain receiving handle, native cancellation signal and remainingMs getter; resolve when drained. Failure is reported and termination proceeds.
Absent: skip application draining work.
stop.drainTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative maximum application drain time; a command graceMs overrides this phase only.
`5000` milliseconds for application drain.
stop.exitTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative wait for actual graceful exit before requesting force.
`5000` milliseconds before force.
stop.reapTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative recovery wait after force; a timed-out unit keeps its lease until actual exit.
`5000` milliseconds of forced recovery.
health: Serial periodic checks for ready handles; consecutive failures invalidate the generation.
Absent: no health monitor is installed.
health.check: Application asynchronous check receiving the current handle and cancellation signal; resolve if healthy, reject or throw to count failure.
health.intervalMs: Finite positive interval between serial checks, measured by the scheduler.
`5000` milliseconds between checks.
health.timeoutMs: Finite nonnegative deadline for one health check before recording failure.
`2000` milliseconds for one check.
health.failureThreshold: Nonnegative safe integer threshold of consecutive failed checks that invalidates readiness.
`3` consecutive failures invalidate the unit.
isolation: Required admission accepts enforced or monitored capabilities; best effort records weaker guarantees as degradation.
`required`; insufficient capabilities fail construction.
requires: Additional capability names chosen by the application, merged with profile requirements before admission.
An empty list adds no capability requirements.
scheduler: Monotonic clock and timers supplied by the application; see `IScheduler` in `@migaia/utils/scheduler`.
`systemScheduler`; uses the host timers.
launcher: Runtime adapter supplied by the application; its launch result must settle exited only after execution and resources stop.
spec: Initial application specification validated by the selected unit profile before admission.
budget: Shared matching-kind budget returned by `createUnitBudget`; actual exit releases its occupied lease.

configuration.name: launcher
configuration.description: `@migaia/supervision/threads` owns a runtime-neutral thread contract. Supply a launcher whose `launch(spec, context)` creates a thread and returns an idempotently terminable handle. Its `exited` promise must fulfill only after thread code stops executing, and must never reject. An error event that leaves a Web-style thread running requires the adapter to terminate it and fulfill `exited` with `{ code: null, error }`. A termination request or a runtime close marker alone is not evidence of actual exit. If `context.signal` is already aborted, the launcher must reject without creating a thread.

symbols.purpose: Application-owned shared admission budget; closing admission does not release live leases.
symbols.core:
kind: Unit kind chosen at budget construction; parent and supervisor kinds must match it.
acquire: Requests a FIFO lease respecting capacity, rate, parent and cancellation. It reserves local capacity before waiting for the parent; reservation is not a started unit. Refusal is data and composite release returns parent before child.
acquire.signal: Optional caller cancellation signal; aborted requests return the aborted reason.
An `IBudgetOutcome`; granted leases must be released after actual exit.
tryAcquire: Attempts immediate admission without joining the wait queue; existing queued callers have precedence.
A synchronous granted lease or stable rejection reason.
inUse: Number of occupied local unit leases; queued requests are counted separately.
pending: Unresolved acquire calls including the active FIFO queue head.
closed: Whether admission has permanently closed; existing occupied leases remain valid.
close: Rejects waiting and future acquisitions; existing leases remain occupied until their owners release them.
Admission is closed; repeated close calls have no further effect.

symbols.name: IThreadSupervisor
symbols.signature: export type IThreadSupervisor<THandle extends IThreadHandle = IThreadHandle> = ISupervisor<THandle, IThreadSpec>;
symbols.purpose: Application-owned command controller for one active execution unit and bounded restart policy.
symbols.core:
state: Current lifecycle state read synchronously without launching or checking the unit.
generation: Attempt generation used to correlate commands and events; it does not count successful restarts.
start: Starts or joins readiness; construction creates no native unit. Startup timeout follows the configured failure policy, while acquireUnit rejection becomes LAUNCH_FAILED with cause even before a lease exists.
An `IReadyOutcome`; disposal rejects with `SCOPE_CLOSED` or `SCOPE_TERMINAL`.
whenReady: Observes stable readiness without starting a new command; cancellation rejects with the caller signal reason.
whenReady.signal: Optional application cancellation signal; abort affects this wait only.
The current `IReadyOutcome`, or rejection on cancellation.
stop: Drains and retires current work; concurrent calls share the pending stop Promise, and the supervisor can later start again.
stop.options: Optional `ISupervisorStopOptions` from the caller; graceMs overrides application drain only.
Resolves after bounded teardown; abandoned actual work retains its lease.
kill: Upgrades the existing teardown to force immediately; joining callers keep the original pending stop Promise.
Resolves after the same bounded stop sequence.
restart: Resets recent restart failures, retires the active unit and launches a fresh attempt.
Readiness outcome for the fresh attempt; disposal rejects with a scope error.
replace: Replaces an active unit with the same or a new spec; invalid strategy throws `INVALID_OPTION` before changing the serving unit.
replace.options: Replacement options: default stop-then-start and current spec. Start-then-switch needs another slot; the serving unit remains owned by its active slot after startup attempt completion. Only candidate readiness and the switched event permit cancelling the old task.
`IReplaceOutcome` reports replacement, admission refusal, or failure without hiding the original error.
inspect: Reads diagnostics without sampling native resources or modifying lifecycle state.
An `ISupervisorSnapshot` of current state and contained failures.
subscribe: Registers a synchronous event observer; it receives `ISupervisorEvent` changes and observer throws are reported.
subscribe.listener: Application callback receives a discriminated event, returns void synchronously, and should not throw.
Idempotent removal function for this observer only.
dispose: Closes admission permanently and joins bounded retirement; repeated in-flight calls share one disposal Promise.
Resolves when disposal reaches its terminal state; future unit-producing commands reject.

symbols.name: IThreadSupervisorOptions
symbols.signature: export type IThreadSupervisorOptions<THandle extends IThreadHandle = IThreadHandle> = ISupervisorBaseOptions<THandle> & { /** * Runtime adapter that creates handles and reports actual exit; the supervisor does not launch * native resources itself. */ readonly launcher: IThreadLauncher<THandle>; /** Initial launch specification validated by the profile before any unit is admitted. */ readonly spec: IThreadSpec; /** Shared unit admission budget; its lease remains occupied until actual unit exit. */ readonly budget: IThreadBudget; };
symbols.purpose: Native worker construction policy sharing the core readiness and lifecycle commands.
symbols.core:
id: Nonempty stable name chosen by the application for diagnostics and durable process ownership.
report: Application callback receiving each contained launch, health, cleanup or late error; returns void synchronously and must not throw. Late health-check failure remains reported after monitor closure; only the exact abort reason is suppressed, and passive failures retain the original object.
ready: Optional asynchronous handshake receiving the launched handle and attempt cancellation signal; resolve to admit readiness, reject or throw to fail startup.
Absent: launch completion is readiness.
startupTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative launch-plus-readiness deadline in scheduler milliseconds; zero expires immediately. Expiry retires the attempt and follows normal restart/terminal policy, publishing a stable outcome instead of leaving the supervisor starting.
`10000` milliseconds for each attempt.
restart: Automatic restart policy for classified exits; nested fields control mode, backoff and the failure window.
An empty policy uses the nested defaults below.
restart.mode: Chooses which actual exits schedule an automatic restart; manual restart remains available.
`on-failure`; normal completion stops.
restart.initialDelayMs: Finite nonnegative first restart delay in scheduler milliseconds.
`250` milliseconds before the first retry.
restart.factor: Finite multiplier of successive restart delays; must be at least one.
`2`; each failure doubles the delay until its cap.
restart.maxDelayMs: Finite nonnegative upper bound of exponential retry delay in milliseconds.
`30000` milliseconds caps backoff.
restart.maxRestarts: Nonnegative safe integer controlling failures admitted in one sliding restart window.
`5` failures before exhaustion.
restart.windowMs: Finite nonnegative scheduler window for counting recent failures.
`60000` milliseconds of failure history.
terminalPolicy: After exhaustion, keeps terminal admission closed or schedules an explicit cooldown.
Absent: remain terminal until explicit restart.
terminalPolicy.mode: Selects a terminal wait until explicit restart or a timed cooldown retry after exhaustion; only disposal permanently closes the supervisor.
terminalPolicy.afterMs: Finite nonnegative cooldown duration required only for the cooldown policy.
stop: Ordered application drain, graceful exit and forced reap phases for each retiring unit.
Absent: each phase uses its nested default.
stop.beforeTerminate: Asynchronous application drain receiving handle, native cancellation signal and remainingMs getter; resolve when drained. Failure is reported and termination proceeds.
Absent: skip application draining work.
stop.drainTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative maximum application drain time; a command graceMs overrides this phase only.
`5000` milliseconds for application drain.
stop.exitTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative wait for actual graceful exit before requesting force.
`5000` milliseconds before force.
stop.reapTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative recovery wait after force; a timed-out unit keeps its lease until actual exit.
`5000` milliseconds of forced recovery.
health: Serial periodic checks for ready handles; consecutive failures invalidate the generation.
Absent: no health monitor is installed.
health.check: Application asynchronous check receiving the current handle and cancellation signal; resolve if healthy, reject or throw to count failure.
health.intervalMs: Finite positive interval between serial checks, measured by the scheduler.
`5000` milliseconds between checks.
health.timeoutMs: Finite nonnegative deadline for one health check before recording failure.
`2000` milliseconds for one check.
health.failureThreshold: Nonnegative safe integer threshold of consecutive failed checks that invalidates readiness.
`3` consecutive failures invalidate the unit.
isolation: Required admission accepts enforced or monitored capabilities; best effort records weaker guarantees as degradation.
`required`; insufficient capabilities fail construction.
requires: Additional capability names chosen by the application, merged with profile requirements before admission.
An empty list adds no capability requirements.
scheduler: Monotonic clock and timers supplied by the application; see `IScheduler` in `@migaia/utils/scheduler`.
`systemScheduler`; uses the host timers.
launcher: Runtime adapter supplied by the application; its launch result must settle exited only after execution and resources stop.
spec: Initial application specification validated by the selected unit profile before admission.
budget: Shared matching-kind budget returned by `createUnitBudget`; actual exit releases its occupied lease.
parameters: This type declaration has no parameters.
symbols.returns: No explicit return annotation is declared for this type.
